source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 6: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.explanation:
Teen components diye hue hain, is liye \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) 3D vector function hoga.
Humein inhein \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ke saath jorna hai aur domain batana hai.
Har component ki apni pabandi hai: fraction mein denominator zero nahin, log ke andar positive, aur inverse secant ke liye \(|t| \ge 1\).
Plan: vector form, phir teeno domains alag alag, phir un ka intersection.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x(t) = \frac{1}{t+4}\), \(y(t) = \ln\sqrt{t}\), \(z(t) = \sec^{-1} t\).
Maloom karna: \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) aur us ka domain.
Tareeqa: 11.1.3 ka Step-2 aur Step-3; domain \(=\) components ke domains ka intersection (11.2.1).

Vector form mein jorein
\[\mathbf{r}(t) = \dfrac{1}{t+4}\,\hat{i} + \ln\sqrt{t}\,\hat{j}\]
\[\quad + \sec^{-1}(t)\,\hat{k}\]
Kyunke \(\ln\sqrt{t} = \ln t^{1/2} = \frac{1}{2}\ln t\), \(\hat{j}\) wala component \(\frac{1}{2}\ln t\) bhi likh sakte hain.
Kyun: \(x, y, z\) ko baari baari \(\hat{i}, \hat{j}, \hat{k}\) ke saath likha. Log ka rule \(\ln a^n = n\ln a\) (jab \(a > 0\)) power ko aage le aata hai, aur square root ki power \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai.

\(x(t) = \frac{1}{t+4}\) ka domain
\[t + 4 \ne 0 \Rightarrow t \ne -4\]
\[\text{domain } \mathbb{R} - \{-4\}\]
Kyun: zero se divide karna defined nahin. Sirf ek number, \(-4\), mana hai; baaki sab theek.

\(y(t) = \ln\sqrt{t}\) ka domain
\(\sqrt{t}\) ke liye \(t \ge 0\); aur \(\ln\) ke liye \(\sqrt{t} > 0\), is liye
\[t > 0,\quad \text{domain } (0, \infty)\]
Kyun: log sirf positive numbers ka hota hai. \(t = 0\) par \(\sqrt{0} = 0\), aur \(\ln 0\) defined nahin, is liye zero bhi bahar.
Dhyan dein: \(t \ge 0\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; yahan sahi \(t > 0\) hai.

\(z(t) = \sec^{-1} t\) ka domain
\[|t| \ge 1\]
\[\text{domain } (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(\sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}\) aur \(\cos\theta\) hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hota hai, is liye \(\sec\theta\) ki value ya to \(1\) ya us se bari, ya \(-1\) ya us se chhoti hoti hai. Inverse secant sirf unhi numbers ka ho sakta hai jo sec ki value ban saken.

Intersection lein
\(y\) se: \(t > 0\). In mein se \(z\) sirf \(t \ge 1\) rehne deta hai; \(t = -4\) to pehle hi bahar hai.
\[\mathbf{r} \text{ ka domain} = [1, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(t\) wahi qabool hai jahan teeno components mojood hon. Number line par teeno domains ko ek doosre ke oopar rakh kar dekhein: teeno ka mushtarka hissa sirf \([1, \infty)\) hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\mathbf{r}(1) = \tfrac{1}{5}\,\hat{i} + 0\,\hat{j} + 0\,\hat{k}\]
mojood hai (\(\ln 1 = 0\), \(\sec^{-1} 1 = 0\)). \(t = \frac{1}{2}\) par \(\sec^{-1}\frac{1}{2}\) defined nahin, is liye \(t = \frac{1}{2}\) ka bahar hona sahi hai \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: \(t = \frac{1}{2}\) par \(x\) aur \(y\) to theek hain, magar ek component bhi na bane to vector nahin banta.
